A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same video-plus-latent ZIG modeling study. Their main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and matchable despite substantial expansion and reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original SENSORIUM prediction, neuron-conditioning, forecasting, and latent–behavior correlation results in Section 3 and the appendices.

after.justification: V2 reports original model evaluations, architectural ablations, cortical maps, neuron-transfer experiments, and out-of-distribution tests in Section 4 and the appendices.

M1.justification: V2 replaces the default GRU latent decoder with direct latent-to-distribution-parameter projections, retaining the earlier decoder as a smoother ablation. It adds coordinate-based MLPs for predicting latent readout weights and transferring them to unseen neurons. V1's autoregressive forecasting variant is removed.

E1.justification: V2 adds out-of-distribution visual stimuli with different spatiotemporal statistics, including pink noise, and prediction for neurons excluded from initial training. Repeated-stimulus controls use recordings from five additional SENSORIUM mice. V1's next-time-step forecasting task is removed.

E2.justification: The primary Poisson and video-only ZIG baselines remain. Comparator changes concern internal model variants: v2 adds coordinate-derived and shared latent-weight alternatives in Table 2 and a CNN smoother in Table 8, while v1's forecasting-trained comparator disappears.

E3.justification: The reported marginalization sample count changes from 5000 in v1 Appendix C to 1000 in v2. New protocols include latent-dimension and conditioning-fraction sweeps with fixed quarter-population evaluation subsets, withholding 500 neurons per mouse followed by readout adaptation, and shuffling conditioning responses across repeated trials.

E4.justification: V2 adds encoder/smoother and pretraining ablations, dimensionality and conditioning-size sensitivity, response-distribution case studies, cortical organization analyses, stimulus-contrast and repeat-shuffling controls, and OOD tests. The existing sampling-convergence analysis gains training-sample experiments. Forecasting analysis is removed.

E5.justification: V2 newly reports SEMs over three initializations in Table 1 and selected ablations, and specifies across-mice SEMs for the CCA summary. V1 Table 1 contains point estimates only. However, v2 Table 3 labels 0.0005/0.0004 as across-mice SEMs, whereas its displayed mouse-level values imply approximately 0.012/0.010.

E6.justification: Table 1's latent log-likelihood changes from -0.74 to -0.30 bits per neuron and time point, while mean correlations remain unchanged. This accompanies model and sampling revisions, rather than establishing a same-setting gain. V2 adds extensive spatial, transfer, sensitivity, and OOD results; Table 5 reports average correlations of 0.08 for Poisson, 0.11 for ZIG, and 0.17 for conditioned latent predictions. Forecasting results are removed.

T1.justification: V2 repairs v1's incomplete ZIG density by explicitly separating uniform and shifted-Gamma regimes. It adds Gaussian projection-variance reasoning for the dimensionality–likelihood relationship and removes the Markov forecasting assumptions and objective. The ELBO and marginalization framework are retained, without new theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: Beyond the retained distribution-prediction and behavior-correlation claims, v2's abstract, introduction, and discussion make unsupervised recovery of cortical topographic organization a principal contribution. The discussion additionally claims that the inferred latents primarily reflect stimulus-independent brain state.

C2.justification: V2 explains the dimensionality-dependent likelihood/correlation tradeoff and interprets spatial organization and neuron transfer. It substantially qualifies the brain-state interpretation: latents may still encode visual information, the biological origin of spatial patterns remains unresolved, and the model requires additional parameters. These extend v1's brief interpretation and future-work discussion.

D1.justification: V2 newly documents moment matching for the Gamma shape parameter, 150 training samples for ELBO estimation, full-video evaluation, pretraining choices, experiment-specific configurations in Table 9, exact mouse IDs and neuron counts in Table 11, and A100/H100 memory constraints. It also states that code will become available upon publication.

R1.justification: V2 expands v1's brief introductory taxonomy into a substantive related-work section discussing deterministic encoders, probabilistic latent models, and recurrent state-space approaches. Added references include Glaser et al. (2020), Li et al. (2023), and Wu et al. (2024). The predictive variational autoencoder reference supporting v1's forecasting extension is removed.

P1.justification: V2 extensively rewrites the abstract, introduction, model description, and discussion, creates a dedicated related-work section, and moves training and marginalization into the main text. The results narrative and appendix organization are substantially restructured beyond the addition of experiments.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a two-column layout, redraws the architecture figure, and adds a problem illustration, sensitivity plots, cortical maps, distribution heatmaps, and numerous experimental and configuration tables. Existing CCA and behavioral trace plots are relocated and reformatted; the forecasting diagram is removed.

improvement.justification: V1 primarily supported its brain-state interpretation through prediction scores and behavior correlations. V2 substantially strengthens that support with contrast and repeat-shuffling controls, architectural and sampling ablations, and OOD and unseen-neuron tests, while explicitly acknowledging possible stimulus leakage and uncertain biological explanations. These gains outweigh removal of the forecasting extension and the new Table 3 uncertainty-reporting inconsistency: the central claims are substantially better tested and qualified.
